The first council of trustees included Gustaf Tamm (chairman), Olof Melin and Olof Björklund from the free traders side, and Filip Boström and Edvard Montgomery from the protectionists.

Among the party's trusted men or more prominent members in the following years are Olof Jonsson i Hof, Carl Swartz, Gustaf Lagerbring and August Wijkander. After the proportional electoral system was applied in 1910 in committee elections, the party's influence was strengthened. In 1910, 46 to 50 members of the 150 members of the chamber gathered around its lists, and it could now also fill a third of the committee seats from its own circle. After the Staaff government in the autumn of 1911 succeeded in obtaining the king's permission to dissolve the first chamber and the left-wing groups returned after it with a strength of 63 men (51 liberals and 12 socialists), a definite desire emerged within the country for a merger of the right-wing groups in the chamber, which led to the dissolution of the Moderate Party and the formation of the First Chamber's National Party at the beginning of the 1912 Riksdag.

parties.relations: Split from the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]] (S) and the [[seKD|Christian Democrats]] (KD)
parties.description:
A Swedish electoral alliance between individual candidates running in the 2024 European Parliament elections. Folklistan was launched by Jan Emanuel, a former [[seSAP|Social Democratic Party]] MP, and Sara Skyttedal, an MEP previously with the [[seKD|Christian Democrats]] in April 2024. They are also the group's main candidates for the European Parliament elections 2024.

Sara Skyttedal was elected Member of the European Parliament in 2019 for the Christian Democrats, who are grouped with the [[euEPP|European People's Party]]. She left the party in February 2024, but remained in parliament as an independent. In early April 2024, it was noticed that she had registered a new party called Folklistan, and it was later launched in Henrik Jönsson's program on YouTube. On June 27, Jan Emanuel announced that the party would be dissolved due to the poor result in the 2024 European Parliament elections.

parties.name: General Suffrage Association of Sweden
parties.relations: Succeeded by the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]] (FL);
parties.description:
A part of the suffrage movement in Sweden, founded in 1890. The leaders of the movement were liberals, but the association was open to all. The previous year, the [[seSAP|Swedish Social Democratic Workers' Party]] had been formed, and when it came to the view on suffrage, the interests of both movements coincided. The symbol used was the cornflower, the national flower of Östergötland, since the two Östergötians Isidor Kjellberg and Alfred Edling were two very strong driving forces in the movement.

The first chairman of the suffrage movement was Julius Mankell, an officer and member of parliament (liberal). On the initiative of the social democrat Hjalmar Branting, the Suffrage Association organized a people's parliament alongside the unjust parliament that had shown itself to be uninterested in universal suffrage. When Mankell died in 1897, the chairmanship was taken over by David Bergström, also a liberal member of parliament. The Swedish General Suffrage Association was dissolved in 1900 and partly succeeded by the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]].

parties.name: Gottland Party Gotland's Future
parties.description:
A local political party founded in 1993 and registered for elections to the municipal council in Gotland Municipality.

GGF was founded in 1993 for the 1994 municipal election.

The party leader was Jan Wiklund.

The party has been represented in Gotland's municipal council during the 1994/1998 and 1998/2002 terms. In the 1994 election, the party received 5.6% of the vote and four seats. During the 1998/2002 term, the party was given a local wave-making role with its three seats. The party governed the municipality with the bourgeois parties in a partnership called "Vi i femman".

In the 2002 election, the party received 756 votes, which corresponded to 2.17%, and lost its mandates. In the 2006 election, the party received 586 votes (1.67%) and also ended up without a mandate in that election. After the election, the party was dissolved.

parties.name: Green Party
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden based on green politics.

Sparked by the anti-nuclear power movement following the 1980 nuclear power referendum, the party was founded in 1981 out of a discontent with the existing parties' environmental policies. In the 1988 general election, they won seats in the Swedish Riksdag for the first time, capturing 5.5 percent of the vote, and becoming the first new party to enter parliament in seventy years. Three years later, they dropped back below the 4 percent threshold.

In 1994, they returned to parliament and have since retained representation there. The party is represented nationally by two spokespeople, always one man and one woman. These roles are currently held by Amanda Lind and Daniel Helldén.

Between 3 October 2014 and 30 November 2021, the Green Party was a part of the [[seSAP|Social Democratic]]-led government. This was the first time the Greens entered government in their history. The Greens left the government after the right-wing opposition parties' budget for 2022 was passed in the Riksdag, and the government's own budget failed to pass.

In the 2018 general election, the Greens received 4.4% of the vote and 16 seats, making the party the smallest in the Riksdag. Despite this, the party was still able to maintain its place in government.

parties.relations: Preceded by the [[seHP|Holstein Party]]
parties.description: Aa Swedish political faction active during the Age of Liberty (1719–1772). Their name derives from the tricorne hat worn by officers and gentlemen. They vied for power with the opposing [[seCaps|Caps]] party. In 18th century Swedish politics, the Hats represented conservatives and the Caps represented liberals. The Hats, who ruled Sweden from 1738 to 1765, advocated an alliance with France and an assertive foreign policy, especially towards Russia. During their tenure, they involved Sweden in two expensive and disastrous wars, in the 1740s and 1750s.

parties.name: Health Care Party
parties.relations: Merger of several regional pro-healthcare organizations (Sveriges sjukvårdspartiers samverkansorganisation, Nätverket för Sveriges sjukvårdspartier) and regional Health Care Parties
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden that was founded in 2005. The party describes itself as a cross-political issue party with health and medical care as its core issues.

The Healthcare Party wants to invest 35 billion kronor more in healthcare and the goal is for healthcare to account for ten percent of the gross domestic product. To finance the proposals, the party proposes, for example, that the increase in the ceiling for health insurance be stopped and that coordination within the social insurance systems be made more efficient.

The party says no to the so-called stop law and wants more private entrepreneurs in healthcare. It also wants to lower employer contributions and, what it calls, the total tax burden.

The party's slogan is: "An Unusual Party for Ordinary People!".

On 19 September 2006, two days after the election, party chairman Kenneth Backgård announced his resignation as the party had not achieved the results it had hoped for. The explanation was that the election had the character of a "presidential election" and that it was therefore extra difficult for upstarts to come forward. The party received 11,519 votes in the election to the Riksdag (0.21 percent of the votes) and thus became the 6th largest party outside the Riksdag.

The party is structured as a coalition party, to which a number of regional and local parties have joined. These are not bound by the coalition party on regional and local issues. Several of the regional parties have existed since 1994.

parties.name: Holstein Party
parties.relations: Succeeded by the [[seHats|Hats Party]]
parties.description:
The party was created in 1718 of those who favored Charles Frederick, Duke of Holstein-Gottorp, son of Charles XII’s elder sister Hedvig Sophia of Sweden, as heir to the throne before that of Ulrika Eleonora, Queen of Sweden.

The party lost to the followers of Ulrika Eleonora in 1719, and to her spouse and successor Frederick I of Sweden in 1720. But due to Frederick I’s plans to strengthen royal power with support of the [[seHov|Hovpartiet]], the Holstein Party were given a favorable situation have Charles Frederick appointed heir to the throne, a situation which was supported by Tsar Peter the Great of Russia who wished influence in Sweden.

In the Riksdag of 1723, the attempt of the king and Hovpartiet to introduce absolute power was crushed and the Holstein Party, whose follower filled the seats of parliament and bought more followers by granting allowances and titles from Holstein and Russia, especially to those losing their property during the Great Northern War: Charles Frederick was granted the title Royal Highness, a Swedish allowance and an informal promise to be considered as heir to the throne should such an election be necessary. The marriage of Charles Frederick to the Russian princess Anna Petrovna and the accession of her mother as Empress Catherine I of Russia in 1725 signified a triumph for the Holstein Party: the rumours that Charles Frederick was about to be appointed Russian heir to the throne or at least be granted the Baltic provinces made him an attractive heir to the Swedish throne by those in Sweden wishing to restore the Swedish Empire, and ambassador Josias Cederhielm was sent to Russia. These plans were however prevented by Arvid Horn with support of the king and the ambassadors of France and Great Britain to prevent Sweden from being involved in a war through Russia's promise to reconquer Slesvig to Holstein from Denmark.

During the Riksdag of 1726-1727, Horn managed to have the Riksdag vote for Sweden to join the Treaty of Hanover (1725) against Russia, and the Holstein followers was removed from the royal council and replaced with the followers of Horn. The defeat of the Holstein Party was completed by the death of Catherine I, which destroyed the power base of Charles Frederick in Russia and forced him to leave for Holstein.

The party's core issues are local democracy, withdrawal from the European Union, the preservation of cash and the Swedish krona, no to Swedish NATO membership and the DCA agreement, freedom of expression and information, holistic public health and health freedom, sustainable agriculture, and a national science-based environmental policy. In both the 2022 parliamentary election and the 2024 European elections, MoD became the fifth largest small party without any mandates.

parties.name: June List
parties.description:
A EU-critical Swedish party, formed in 2004, which was occasionally represented in the European Parliament. The party has been mothballed since 2014, the same year that the current party leader Jörgen Appelgren, who succeeded Birgitta Swedenborg, took office. The party's name comes from the fact that the party was founded before the European Parliament elections in June 2004 and then consisted only of the people on the ballot. The June List became Sweden's third largest party in the European elections in June 2004 with 14.5 percent of the vote, and thus received three seats in the European Parliament.

In the 2009 European Parliament elections, the party was led by Sören Wibe, but the party received only 3.6 percent of the vote and thus left the parliament. Wibe died unexpectedly in 2010 and the party was then "mothballed". The party was revived in February 2014 for the European Parliament elections that year, with a new list led by Jörgen Appelgren. Now it did not achieve more than 0.3% of the vote. On 27 October 2014, the party wrote on its website that the party had once again been mothballed.

description.text:
A EU-critical Swedish party, formed in 2004, which was occasionally represented in the European Parliament. The party has been mothballed since 2014, the same year that the current party leader Jörgen Appelgren, who succeeded Birgitta Swedenborg, took office. The party's name comes from the fact that the party was founded before the European Parliament elections in June 2004 and then consisted only of the people on the ballot. The June List became Sweden's third largest party in the European elections in June 2004 with 14.5 percent of the vote, and thus received three seats in the European Parliament.

In the 2009 European Parliament elections, the party was led by Sören Wibe, but the party received only 3.6 percent of the vote and thus left the parliament. Wibe died unexpectedly in 2010 and the party was then "mothballed". The party was revived in February 2014 for the European Parliament elections that year, with a new list led by Jörgen Appelgren. Now it did not achieve more than 0.3% of the vote. On 27 October 2014, the party wrote on its website that the party had once again been mothballed.

parties.name: Knapptryckarna
parties.description:
A Swedish political party, founded in 2021. The party advocates direct democracy where citizens vote directly on every issue instead of the current system of representative democracy.

Knapptrykarna was founded in 2021 by musician and entrepreneur Ulf Bejerstrand. Their symbol was originally a stylized voting button in the form of a red and green striped ring.

In Forshaga municipality in Värmland, three [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] left the party after internal battles in the party region in 2023. They then stated that they would represent Knapptrykarna. One of them, Jan-Erik Tjärngård, explained that "the idea is that we should be able to post questions that people can think about, so that they can have a say. Then we can represent that opinion, regardless of what we ourselves think". When asked directly whether he would follow the results of the votes even in cases where they conflict with his own convictions, he replied that he would decide on a "case-by-case basis". The exact design of the voting system was also unclear. An editorial in Värmlands Folkblad described it as "a conspiracy of the tinfoil hats".

Knapptryckarna ran an active campaign ahead of the 2022 parliamentary elections. During Almedalen Week in Visby, they handed out flyers and popcorn. They argued for a referendum on Swedish NATO membership. They received 5,493 votes, which corresponds to 0.08 percent of all votes. This made them the country's 15th largest party and the seventh largest outside the Riksdag.

The Knapptrykkarna did not list any candidates for the 2024 European elections, nor did the party print any ballots. However, one of the party's members, Dick Jonefelt from Färgelanda, was in seventh place on the ballot for the party [[seMoD|Human Rights and Democracy]]. The Knapptrykkarna received a total of 80 votes.

parties.name: Lantmanna Party
parties.relations:
In 1888–1895 collapsed into [[seNLmp|New Lantmanna Party]] and [[seGLmp|Old Lantmanna Party]];

Merged into the [[seLABP|Farmers' and Bourgeoisie Party]] (LABP)
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden during the late 19th century, essentially a faction in the parliament which existed from 1867 to 1912 (though split in two 1888–1895). The Lantmanna Party was founded in 1867, following the representation reform of 1866 which had replaced the old Riksdag of the Estates with the modern Riksdag, assembled for the first time in early 1867. It was represented in the second chamber (Andra kammaren) of the parliament, which was directly elected.

The party originally did not have any clear political ideology but claimed to represent farmers and ordinary people, although it was never a real agrarian party. Many of its first members had been members of the last Estate of Peasants in the old Riksdag of the Estates while one of the informal leaders at the start was Count Arvid Posse. The party was also supported by the main Swedish newspaper at the time, Dagens Nyheter. Posse went on to become Prime Minister of Sweden from 1880 to 1883.

In 1888 the party was split in two parties over the issue on free trade contra protectionism; the free trade advocates founded the [[seGLmp|Old Lantmanna Party]] and the protectionists founded the [[seNLmp|New Lantmanna Party]]. In 1895 the two parties reunited under its old name. Erik Gustaf Boström of the Lantmanna Party (New Lantmanna Party during the split) was able to form a cabinet twice, as prime minister in 1891–1900 and again in 1902–1905.

By the turn of the century 1900, the party had evolved in an ideologically conservative way, much due to opposition against the [[seLibs|liberals]] and the emerging [[seSAP|social democrats]]. While the party had its base in the parliament and was formed solely by elected members of it, there was no organisation for election campaigns until 1904, when the Lantmanna Party formed the [[seAVM|General Electoral League]] together with other right-wing fractions in the parliament. In 1912 the Lantmanna Party merged with another of the right-wing fractions of the parliament, the [[seNFP|National Progress Party]], to form the new [[seLABP|Farmer and Bourgeoisie Party]], which came to be known as the andrakammarshögern ('right-wing faction of the second chamber'). This and the Allmänna valmansförbundet eventually evolved into the present [[seM|Moderate Party]].

parties.name: Left Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seSAP|Swedish Social Democratic Workers' Party]] (SAP)
parties.description:
A socialist political party in Sweden. On economic issues, the party opposes privatisations, and advocates for increased public expenditures. In foreign policy, the party is Eurosceptic, being critical of the European Union, NATO, and opposing Sweden's entry into the eurozone. It attempted to get Sweden to join the Non-Aligned Movement in 1980, but did not succeed. The party is eco-socialist, and supports republicanism. It stands on the far left-wing of the political spectrum.

The party has never been part of a government at the national level; however, it has lent parliamentary support to governments led in the Riksdag by the [[seSAP|Swedish Social Democratic Party]]. From 1998 to 2006, the Left Party was in a confidence and supply arrangement with the ruling Social Democrats and the [[seMP|Green Party]]. Between 2014 and 2018, it supported the minority government of Social Democrats and Greens in the Riksdag, extending this cooperation to many of Sweden's counties and municipalities; and from 2018 to 2021, until the outset of the 2021 Swedish government crisis, it offered passive support to the Löfven II cabinet formed under the January Agreement, though disagreeing with some of the policies mandated by the Agreement.

The party originates from the split of the Social Democrats in 1917, into the Swedish Social Democratic Left Party (SSV), becoming the Communist Party of Sweden in 1921. In 1967, the party was renamed to Left Party – the Communists (VPK); it adopted its current name in 1990. The Left Party is a member of the [[euNGLA|Nordic Green Left Alliance]], and its two MEPs sit in The Left in the European Parliament (GUE/NGL) group. In 2018, the party joined [[euNTP|Now the People!]]. It is also part of the [[euELA|European Left Alliance for the People and the Planet]], a European political party that supports an alternative to capitalism.

parties.name: Left Socialist Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seSSP|Socialist Party]] (SP)
parties.description:
A left-wing political party in Sweden that existed between 1940 and 1963.

Albin Ström was a leftwing Social Democrat from Gothenburg who led a split from the [[seSAP|Social Democratic Party]] in 1934, taking with him a few thousand members from the West Coast region. The tendency of Ström founded the daily Arbetarposten (Workers' Mail) and quickly aligned itself with Karl Kilbom and Nils Flyg's splinter [[seSSP|Communist Party]] (not aligned to Moscow). These currents were united to form [[seSSP|Socialist Party]]. When SP, under the leadership of Nils Flyg, gradually orientated itself towards Nazism, many of its members left the party. The tendency of Ström broke away in 1940 and formed Vänstersocialistiska Partiet, after that Flyg had promoted that the SKP were to be suppressed by the state. VSP became very much centered on Ström and his group in Gothenburg.

Arbetarposten was the main publication of the VSP, with Ström as editor. The paper was founded in 1934. During the war, it suffered from several persecutions from the government and the paper was confiscated 24 times. During the war, it had a print run of around 1,000, which rose to around 1,500 after the war. The paper was mainly distributed in Gothenburg, and to a lesser degree in Borås. Arbetarposten ceased publication in 1961. With Ström's death in 1963, the party dissolved.

In 1945, a group of VSP militants, including Evald Höglund (who later formed the trotskyist [[seRSP|RSP]]) and Anton Nilson, left the party due to their perception of the party taking a pro-Western Bloc position.

parties.name: Liberal Coalition Party
parties.relations:
Preceded by the [[seFP|People's Party]] (FP) and various discussion clubs;

Parliamentary group of the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]] (FL)
parties.description:
A parliamentary group of the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]] in Swedish Parliament. It was founded in 1900 from a coalition of reform-minded parliamentarians from Parliamentary [[seFP|People's Party]] and others, such as rural discussion clubs and part of the [[seLmp|Lantmanna Party]]. It quickly became influential and in 1902 founded its nationwide political party, the Free-minded National Association. Its new liberal progamme was characterized by advocating for universal male suffrage and parliamentary democracy. Under leaders like Sixten von Friesen and later Karl Staaff, the parliamentary party gained power and formed governments, working closely with the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]]. Key reforms included constitutional changes and expanded voting rights, though internal disagreements—especially over defense policy and prohibition—eventually weakened the party.

After Staaff’s death in 1915, leadership passed to Nils Edén, who led a coalition government that implemented major democratic reforms. However, tensions between the party’s rural, pro-prohibition wing and its urban, culturally liberal faction deepened. These internal divisions culminated in a formal split of parliamentarians from newly founded Liberal Party of Sweden in 1923. As a result, the Liberal Coalition Party dissolved, ending its role in Swedish politics. Free-minded National Association named its new parliamentary caucus as [[seFF|Free-minded People's Party]], while [[seSLP|Liberal Party of Sweden]] founded parliamentary caucus called [[seLR|Liberal Riksdag Party]].

parties.name: Liberal Party of Sweden
parties.description:
A political party that from 1923 to 1934 functioned as the party organization for the parliamentary [[seLR|Liberal Riksdag Party]] .

It was formed during the National Assembly of the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]] on 27 May 1923. The issue of prohibition of intoxicants shattered this party, although other factors, such as personal issues, also played a role. The minority opposed to prohibition, mainly in southern Sweden, left the party and formed the Liberal Party of Sweden after the National Assembly decided to continue to campaign for prohibition, despite the fact that a majority of voters in the referendum on prohibition of intoxicants in Sweden said no to this.

The party merged with the Free-minded National Association in 1934 under the name of the [[seL|People's Party]].

parties.name: Liberal Riksdag Party
parties.description:
A parliamentary party affiliated with the [[seSLP|Liberal Party of Sweden]]. It was formed on 10 January 1924 by opponents of alcohol prohibition who had left the [[seLibs|Liberal Coalition Party]] in connection with the party's dissolution in May 1923. Initially, the party comprised 20 members of parliament (14 in the first chamber and 6 in the second chamber) but gradually merged so that only 6 remained.

The party ceased to exist when it merged with the [[seFF|Free-minded People's Party]] in 1935 under the name of the [[seL|People's Party]].

parties.relations: Merger of the [[seFL|Free-minded National Association]] (FL) and the [[seSLP|Liberal Party of Sweden]] (SLP)
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden generally described as liberal or conservative-liberal. The party is a member of the Liberal International and Renew Europe.

The Liberals are considered centre-right, but have historically been situated in the centre of the Swedish political landscape. Since the leadership of Lars Leijonborg and Jan Björklund in the 2000s, the party has increasingly adopted more conservative-liberal positions.

Since 2022, the Liberals have been a junior partner in the Kristersson cabinet, a centre-right coalition with the Moderate Party and the Christian Democrats, which relies on the parliamentary support of the far-right Sweden Democrats.

parties.name: Liquor Party
parties.description:
A Swedish single-issue party that wants to halve the alcohol consumption of Swedes within ten years from 2010. It was founded by Benny Haag in the autumn of 2009. It had no seats in the Riksdag, county councils or municipal councils.

The party's spokespeople were Benny Haag and Pär Carlsson. In the 2010 Riksdag election, the party received 237 votes and became the thirteenth largest party outside the Riksdag. Before the election, the party received some media attention, including when the party's founder urged people to vote for the party in a debate article in Aftonbladet, and when Mats Olsson in Expressen announced that he intended to vote for the Alcohol Party.

parties.name: Marxist–Leninist Struggle League
parties.relations:
Preceded by the Left Youth League (VUF), the youth wing of the [[seVPK|VPK]], which split from it in 1968;

Merged into the Röd Ungdom, the youth organization of [[seKFML|Communist Party of Sweden]] (SKP).
parties.description:
A communist political organization in Sweden formed in 1970 by Vänsterns Ungdomsförbund (Left Youth League), the youth organization of [[seVPK|VPK]]. Within VUF several ultraleftist tendencies had surged during the 1960s, orientating it toward Maoism. VUF broke with VPK in 1968; in 1970, they formed MLK. MLK was ideologically almost identical with the larger KFML/SKP, with Marxism–Leninism-Mao Zedong Thought as the ideological backbone. MLK supported [[seKFML|KFML/SKP]] in elections.

Notable former members include later Left Party leader Gudrun Schyman.

MLK suffered a major split in 1972 when a group under leadership of Anders Carlberg (had been the chairman of VUF) left MLK and formed Förbundet KOMMUNIST (League COMMUNIST).

MLK published Stormklockan, Kommunistisk Tidskrift för marxistisk-leninistisk teori och praktik and Suomalainen Stormklockan (in Finnish). The two latter ones were published between 1971 and 1978. Between 1980 and 1982, MLK and Kommunistisk Ungdom, the new VPK youth organisation, were involved in a legal dispute over the right to publish newspapers using the name Stormklockan, with MLK winning the dispute in the Court of Appeal for Western Sweden.[2]

MLK maintained four bookstores, named after Set Persson, in Stockholm, Trollhättan, Sundsvall and Kiruna.

In 1981-1983, MLK unified itself with Röd Ungdom, the youth organization of [[seKFML|SKP]].

parties.name: Moderate Party
parties.description:
A liberal-conservative political party in Sweden. The party generally supports tax cuts, the free market, civil liberties and economic liberalism. Globally, it is a full member of the [[intIDU|International Democracy Union]] and the [[euEPP|European People's Party]].

The party was founded in 1904 as the General Electoral League by a group of conservatives in the Riksdag, the Swedish parliament. The party was later known as The Right and The Right Party. During this time, the party was usually called the Conservative Party and adhered to a purely conservative and nationalistic ideologies, whereas today its ideology combines conservative and liberal ideas.

After holding minor posts in centre-right governments, the Moderates eventually became the leading opposition party to the [[seSAP|Swedish Social Democratic Party]] and since then those two parties have dominated Swedish politics. After the 1991 Swedish general election, party leader Carl Bildt formed a minority government, the first administration since 1930 to be headed by a member of the party, which lasted three years. The party returned to government under leader and Prime Minister Fredrik Reinfeldt, after the 2006 and 2010 general elections. In 2010, the party was the leading member of the [[seAlliansen|Alliance]], a centre-right coalition, along with the [[seC|Centre Party]] (C), the [[seKD|Christian Democrats]] (KD) and the [[seL|Liberal People's Party]] (FP), and obtained its best result ever (30.1%), despite the coalition not being able to obtain majority.

The current chairman of the party, Ulf Kristersson, was elected at a special party congress on 1 October 2017, following Anna Kinberg Batra's sudden resignation. Kinberg Batra had replaced Reinfeldt, Prime Minister from 2006 to 2014. Under Reinfeldt's leadership, the party moved more towards the centre. Under Kristersson's leadership, the party moved back to the right and opened up to the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] (SD) following the 2018 Swedish general election. Having formed in late 2021 an informal right-wing alliance with SD and former Alliance members, KD and L, with Kristersson as the prime ministerial candidate, the right-wing bloc obtained a narrow win in the 2022 Swedish general election.

parties.name: National Agrarian Union
parties.relations: Merged into the [[seC|Farmers' League]] (BF)
parties.description:
An agrarian political party in Sweden, one of the fore-runners of the [[seC|Centre Party]].

JR was founded on 6 February 1915, the anniversary of the 1914 Farmers' March. Among the founders of JR were several of the 1914 Farmers' March participants. Soon after the foundation of the party, the Swedish Farmers' League and the Scanian Farmers' League merged into it. Johannes Nilsson i Gårdsby became the party chairman. Vårt land och folk ('Our country and people'), with Elfrid Dürango as its editor, became the party press organ. Member of parliament Nils Johansson i Brånalt became a prominent leader of the party. JR was mainly concentrated in Skåne, Östergötland, as well as to a lesser extent, Värmland and Jämtland.

Compared to the other agrarian party, the [[seC|Farmers' League]], JR was politically further to the right and represented larger estate owners. Later Centre Party historiography has sought to downplay differences between the two parties, but JR and the Farmers' League were rivals for the rural vote. JR had a nationalist outlook with racial overtones (including a fierce opposition to Jewish immigration). Both parties opposed female suffrage and introduction of equal voting rights for local elections (although the Farmers' League revised its policy on local elections by 1918). In the 1917 elections, the Farmers' League won 9 seats and JR 5 seats. After the election, JR began calling for unity between the two parties but the Farmers' League initially resisted the proposition. JR proposed forming a joint parliamentary faction, but after the Farmers' League declined the offer JR established the 'Free Agrarian Group' in the parliament on 17 January 1918, with Olof Olsson i Kullenbergstorp as the chairman of the new parliamentary faction. The two parties merged in 1921, keeping the name of the [[seC|Farmers' League]] (which in the 1950s took the name 'Centre Party').

parties.name: National Democrats
parties.relations: Split from the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] (SD)
parties.description:
A far-right, nationalist political party in Sweden, formed in 2001 as a breakaway from the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]]. Before the dissolution, the National Democrats had two municipal council seats in Södertälje Municipality and one in Heby Municipality (the defected Sweden Democrat Carina Bergman). The party has previously held seats in Nykvarn Municipality (Daniel Spansk was elected in 2006 but left the party in 2011 in protest against party leader Abramsson) as well as in Tranemo Municipality (the vice-chairman of the Democratic Alliance Thomas Bengtström who defected in May 2010) and Trollhättan Municipality (with the 2011 expelled Sweden Democrat Thomas Karlsén).

The party leader was Marc Abramsson from 2007 to 2014. The party published the newspaper Nationell Idag, which in 2014 became independent as an unaffiliated Sweden Democrat. The party's youth wing was called Nationaldemokratisk Ungdom (NDU). Previously, there was also a women's association, the National Women's Association. The National Democrats have demonstrated together with openly neo-Nazi organizations such as the [[seNMR|Swedish Resistance Movement]] and the [[seNSF|National Socialist Front]].

On 23 April 2014, Marc Abramsson announced that the party would cease its activities at the national level and would not stand in the 2014 elections. He also urged those "looking for an outlet for activism" to seek out Nordic Youth. Former ND member Mikael Johansson became leader of the Swedish section of Soldiers of Odin in 2016.

parties.name: National Progress Party
parties.relations:
Split from the [[seLmp|Lantmanna Party]];

Merged into the [[seLABP|Farmers' and Bourgeoisie Party]] (LABP)
parties.description:
A moderate conservative party in the second chamber that was formed in 1906 through a breakaway from the [[seLmp|Lantmanna Party]]. The chairman was Hans Andersson i Nöbbelöv.

The National Progress Party's goal was to unite the common interests of the countryside and the cities in a better way than in the rural-dominated Lantmanna Party. The number of members of parliament was 42 at the time of its founding, but gradually decreased to 30 in 1911. After the second chamber election in 1911, the party reunited with the Lantmanna Party in 1912 under the new name [[seLABP|Farmers' and Bourgeoisie Party]], which came to be called "the second chamber right". The National Progress Party is thus one of the historical predecessors of the [[seM|Moderate Coalition Party]].

parties.name: National Socialist Front
parties.relations:
Preceded by the [[seVAM|White Aryan Resistance]] (VAM) militant neo-Nazi network;

Succeeded by the [[seFoF|People's Front]] (FF)
parties.description:
At the time of its dissolution the largest Neo-Nazi political party in Sweden. The organization was founded in Karlskrona on 8 August 1994. It became a political party on 20 April 1999, the 110th birthday of Adolf Hitler. The party's official newspaper—now defunct—was named Den Svenske Nationalsocialisten ("The Swedish National Socialist"), also known as Den Svenske ("The Swedish").

The party ran in the municipal council elections in Karlskrona in 2002, but only attracted 0.5% of the votes which was not sufficient for a mandate. In 2006 the party entered the elections at a national level. There it gained 1,417 votes, or 0.03% (in order to enter the Swedish parliament a party needs at least 4% of the total votes). The party was most successful in Trollhättan, where it received 208 votes or 0.65%, although this was not enough to enter the municipal assembly. 2006 was the best election year in the party's history.

In 2007, the NSF demonstrated in Stockholm for the release of Holocaust denier Ernst Zündel.

The National Socialist Front had a mandatory political uniform dress code during marches and demonstrations, which included a black combat-sweater or shirt, black military-cap, boots, khaki-coloured combat pants and the party's logo on the arms. This uniform was taken out of use after the police stated in 2006 that it was a hate crime to wear them during demonstrations. The members of the party often wore a blue T-shirt with yellow text that said "NSF" after this.
parties.ideology: The party had as its main goals the abolition of democracy, the repatriation of immigrants, internment of communists into work camps, a repeat of the Holocaust and the implementation of scientific racism and cutting taxes for families with many genetically healthy children. The NSF also launched a campaign to defend Mel Gibson over the criticism he received from Abraham Foxman for making the film The Passion of the Christ.

parties.name: New Democracy
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden. It was founded in 1991 and elected into the Riksdag in the 1991 Swedish general election. It lost all its seats in the Riksdag in the subsequent election in 1994, and its subsequent decline culminated in bankruptcy in February 2000, at which time it retained only one city council post. Local factions of New Democracy reformed into minor parties such as Sjöbopartiet, which experienced mixed success.

New Democracy campaigned on an agenda of reform and restricted immigration, initially on economic rather than cultural grounds. Its economic policy, stressing the importance of entrepreneurship and deregulation, was generally perceived as right-wing. The party favored Swedish application for European Union membership, which was attained in 1995. It also called for wide-scale political reform, including cutting government departments, reducing the Riksdag to 151 members and electing the Prime Minister by direct ballot.

These years were the only time a right-wing populist party had been represented in the Riksdag until the election of members of the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] in September 2010.

parties.name: New Future
parties.description:
A eurosceptic political party in Sweden. It was founded before the 1994 parliamentary elections in an attempt to prevent Sweden from joining the European Union. After Sweden joined the EU, the party changed its political position and declared their goal to get Sweden to leave the EU, and instead creating a deeper co-operation with Norway and Finland, in a movement reminiscent of Scandinavism. In the 2002 parliamentary elections, it received 9,337 votes, making it the tenth largest party outside of the Swedish parliament; it received 1,171 votes in the 2006 elections.

The party has not campaigned in any elections since 2006.

parties.description:
A Neo-Nazi political party in Sweden, founded in 1956 as the National Socialist Combat League of Sweden (Sveriges nationalsocialistiska kampförbund) by Göran Assar Oredsson. Oredsson was also the party leader except for a few years during the 1970s while he wrote his autobiography Prisat vare allt som gjort mig hårdare ("Blessed be everything that has made me a harder man"). During that time, his wife Vera Oredsson took on the role as party leader and became Sweden's first female party leader.

The party had a group modelled after the German Sturmabteilung, called the Realm Action Group (Swedish: Riksaktionsgruppen, RAG). whose members committed several political crimes. NRP published a few magazines, two being the "Nordic Struggle" and "The Sunwheel".

In 1973, NRP ran for the Swedish parliament but only obtained a few hundred votes. In 2009, the party dissolved.

parties.relations: Preceded by the [[seVAM|White Aryan Resistance]] (VAM) militant neo-Nazi network.
parties.description: A pan-Nordic neo-Nazi movement in the Nordic countries and a political party in Sweden. Besides Sweden, it is established in Norway, Denmark and Iceland, and formerly in Finland before it was banned in 2019. Terrorism expert Magnus Ranstorp has described the NRM as a terrorist organization due to their aim of abolishing democracy along with their paramilitary activities and weapons caches. In 2022, some members of the United States Congress began calling for the organization to be added to the United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations. On 14 June 2024, the United States Department of State designated NRM and its leaders as Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGT).

parties.name: Nuance Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seC|Centre Party]] (C)
parties.description: A political party in Sweden. It was founded in 2019 with the aim of representing minority groups with foreign backgrounds, especially the country's Muslim population. In the 2022 local election, the party won three municipal seats, one in Landskrona and two in Botkyrka. The party has been criticized due to allegedly defending former ISIS members. The leader of the party has stated his defence as being based on human rights and the lack of public evidence against the alleged offenders.

parties.name: Örebro Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seV|Left Party]]
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden. The party was initially active only in Örebro, but has since sought to become a national party by entering the Riksdag. Markus Allard is the party leader. According to Allard, the party cannot be placed anywhere on the traditional left–right political spectrum. The party has variously been characterized as left-wing, right-wing, populist, nationalist, and conservative.

Some key issues for the Örebro Party locally include strong secularism, a 30-hour workweek with retained pay, lowered wages for politicians, expanded social housing, abolishing preschool fees, making public transport free of charge, ending taxpayer funding of what it sees as wasteful sculptures, monuments and art and introducing free dental care. Nationally the party has set out large-scale remigration, closing the Swedish borders to immigration, a stricter assimilation policy and ending taxes on energy and fuel as some of its key issues. The party runs candidates for seats in the municipal assembly of Örebro Municipality and the Örebro County Council. Since the 2022 elections, it has held five seats in the municipal assembly and three in the regional assembly. Its symbol represents Svampen (The Mushroom), a water tower that is a prominent landmark in Örebro.

In October 2025, party leader Markus Allard announced the party's intention to contest the 2026 Swedish general election. Allard said the decision was motivated by the party's financial position, which now allowed it to field candidates in the election to the Riksdag. He set a goal of winning a seat in parliament through the Örebro Riksdag constituency, where the electoral threshold is 12%.

parties.name: Party of the Swedes
parties.relations: Preceded by the [[seNSF|National Socialist Front]] (NSF)
parties.description:
A neo-Nazi political party in Sweden. From 2013 to 2015, the party leader was Stefan Jacobsson. The party dissolved on 10 May 2015 due to lack of members.

The Ægishjálmur rune was the official SVP symbol since it originated as People's Front (Folkfronten), a neo-Nazi party founded in 2008 by members of the [[seNSF|National Socialist Front]] (NSF), the largest Swedish neo-Nazi party at the time. The current name was introduced in 2009 after socialist activists registered NSF's name with the Election Authority of Sweden, blocking its use.

The party's only electoral success was one municipal mandate in 2010 in the small community of Grästorp in Västra Götaland in western Sweden. The mandate was lost after it was revealed that their representative, Daniel Höglund, was not registered as a resident, which is a requirement for members of municipal councils in Sweden. In the 2014 general election the party polled 0.07% with 4,189 votes. The decision to disband came seven months later.
parties.ideology: The party described itself as nationalist and sought to limit Swedish citizenship only to individuals who belong to the "Western genetic and cultural legacy".

parties.name: People's Party
parties.relations: Succeeded by the [[seLibs|Liberal Coalition Party]] (Lib s)
parties.description: A liberal parliamentary party in the second chamber of the Swedish Riksdag. The party was formed on 29 April 1895 by 32 members of parliament. The People's Party's program was written by Fridtjuv Berg and David Bergström, and the party's chairman was Jöns Bromée. About half were radical liberals from the Stockholm area, but the group also had a strong element of farmers from Norrland and Dalarna. On 16 January 1900, the People's Party joined the newly formed Liberal Coalition Party.

parties.name: Pirate Party
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden founded in 2006. Its sudden popularity has given rise to parties with the same name and similar goals across Europe and worldwide, forming the [[intIPP|International Pirate Party]] movement.

The Pirate Party was initially formed to reform laws regarding copyright and patents. The party agenda includes support for strengthening the individual's right to privacy, both on the Internet and in everyday life, and the transparency of state administration. The Pirate Party has intentionally chosen to be bloc independent of the traditional left-right scale to pursue their political agenda with all mainstream parties. The party originally stayed neutral on other matters, but started broadening into other political areas in 2012.

The Pirate Party participated in the 2006 Riksdag elections and gained 0.63% of the votes, making them the third largest party outside parliament. In terms of membership, it passed the [[seMP|Green Party]] in December 2008, the Left Party in February 2009, the [[seL|Liberal People's Party]] and the [[seKD|Christian Democrats]] in April 2009, and the [[seC|Centre Party]] in May 2009, making it, for the time being, the third largest political party in Sweden by membership. The Pirate Party's associated youth organisation, Young Pirate (Swedish: Ung Pirat), was, for a part of 2009 and 2010, the largest political youth organisation in Sweden by membership count.

The Pirate Party came fifth in the 2009 European Parliament elections with 7.13% of the vote and one MEP (increasing to two after ratification of the Lisbon Treaty). Christian Engström became the first MEP for the party, and Amelia Andersdotter took the second seat on 1 December 2009.

Rick Falkvinge, founder of the party, stepped down on 1 January 2011 after five years as party leader, making vice leader Anna Troberg the party leader.

On 1 December 2014, Anna Troberg announced that she would not be available for re-election in 2015 after her term ended on 31 December 2014.

During the autumn meeting in 2024 Mikael Enmalm was elected party leader and Kevin Stenberg was elected secretary general of the party.

parties.name: Progress Party
parties.relations:
Merger of the [[seMbS|Civic Assembly]] (MbS) and the [[seSfF|Assembly for Progress]];

In 1987, partially merged into the [[seSveP|Sweden Party]]
parties.description:
The Progress Party was a Swedish right-wing populist party, formed in 1968 from the remnants of the [[seMbS|Civic Assembly]] (MbS) and the [[seSfF|Assembly for Progress]]. These two parties were originally attempts at bourgeois cooperation and had their main base in Skåne. They saw themselves as a Swedish equivalent to the [[noFrP|Progress Party]] in Norway and the [[dkFrP|Progress Party]] in Denmark.

During the 1980s, the party developed in a xenophobic direction. In 1986, the party ceased to exist at the national level when it merged with [[seBSS|Bevara Sverige Svenskt]] to form the [[seSveP|Sweden Party]], a collaboration that was later terminated. Former Progress Party members instead participated in the founding of the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] in 1988. However, the Progress Party survived in a few municipalities until the mid-2000s.

The party was founded under the leadership of former MP Bertil Rubin, who had previously been active in the [[seC|Centre Party]]. The goal was initially to put up a broad campaign for the local elections in 1970, but due to a lack of funding, the actual campaign was rather modest. This led to a significant loss of blood in the organization.

However, they had managed to take some local mandates and some local branches continued their activities, for example in Motala and Stockholm, under the leadership of Stefan Herrmann. However, the party organization never became stable and was plagued by internal strife and defections. The party mainly pursued issues such as tax cuts and demands for cheaper alcohol. However, from the beginning of the 1980s, the immigration issue became increasingly important and in particular the Stockholm branch with Stefan Herrmann took a critical stance.

The change in orientation led to even greater internal tensions, which ended with the group around Herrmann leaving the Progress Party and instead forming the [[seSveP|Sweden Party]].

The remainder of the party gathered before the 1985 election around Tony Wiklander, an established municipal politician in Åstorp who had defected from [[seVPK|VPK]] and previously from the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]] and who ran a local party, the Löntagarepartiet. Together with other local parties with a primary base in Skåne, the Progress Party continued to operate, with some success at the local level in various municipalities.

Municipal representation was obtained in Motala 1985–1988, Åstorp 1985–2002, Bjuv 1988–2006, Helsingborg 1991–1994 and Landskrona 1994–2002.

In the 1991 parliamentary election, [[seNyD|New Democracy]] ran with a similar policy, which led to the Progress Party's main financier Carl Lundström stopping supporting the party. The Helsingborg branch was first transformed into Svensk Samling and merged with the Sweden Democrats in 1998. Before the 1998 election, the Progress Party branch in Älvkarleby joined the Sweden Democrats, a branch that had received one of FsP's few mandates. The Älvkarleby branch was then in a dispute with Tony Wiklander over who was elected party leader, Wiklander or Gun-Britt Holmgren. Some former Progress Party members joined the SD and closed down their local party Svensk Samling after failing in the 1998 election.

Other municipal branches, including party leader Tony Wiklander's branch in Åstorp, waited until after the split of the Sweden Democrats in 2001 to then join the Sweden Democrats. Other people who had previously been active in the Progress Party switched to the [[seND|National Democrats]].

In Åstorp, Kommunens framtid was formed as a replacement for the 2002 election. Tony Wiklander was on the SD's parliamentary list.

parties.name: Revolutionary Communist Party
parties.relations: Founded by the Marxist newspaper Revolution, Swedish section of the [[intIMT|IMT]].
parties.description:
A Swedish section of the [[intRCI|Revolutionary Communist International]]. The RKP stands for a complete transformation of society and for capitalism to be replaced by socialism, which is the rule of the working class.

The RKP believes that society must come to terms with the entire current system and the wealth of the ruling class by nationalizing the most important parts of the economy – the banks, the mines and the large monopolies – under the democratic control and rule of the workers, and run them according to a social production plan in order to use society's resources and modern technology to eliminate unemployment and reduce working hours. Their parent organization (RCI) has sections in over 30 countries around the world.

parties.name: Revolutionary Socialist Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seVSP|Left Socialist Party]] (VSP)
parties.description:
A Swedish Trotskyist political party founded in 1945, as the Independent Labour Party. It was founded by a group that had split from the [[seVSP|Left Socialist Party]] (VSP), when VSP had developed in a pro-Western direction. Leaders included Evald Höglund and Gottfrid Nyberg.

OAP published two issues of Vårt Ord.

In 1949, the group was reconstructed as Revolutionary Socialists. RS became the first Swedish section of the [[seFI|Fourth International]]. The following year it changed name to RSP at a conference in Stockholm. The group gathered around a dozen persons.

RSP was active in the 1950 municipal elections in Stockholm (where they received 1,900 votes) and during the dockers' strike of 1951. RSP published two issues of Internationalen.

RSP was a short-lived party. Soon the leadership of FI ordered RSP to enter [[seSAP|SAP]] and practice fraction politics, entryism, within this party. The members of RSP opposed this, and the organization was dissolved in 1953.

parties.name: Royal Court Party
parties.description: A political group in Sweden during the Age of Liberty. Its stated objective was to strengthen the influence and power of the monarchy against the Riksdag of the Estates. It is most known in history as the force behind Queen Louisa Ulrika's Coup of 1756, but it did in fact exist in some form or another from 1723 until Gustav III's Revolution of 1772, when its unstated objective of reinstating an absolute monarchy was finally realized.

parties.name: Scania Party
parties.description:
An autonomist, right-wing populist, regionalist, anti-immigration political party based in the Swedish province of Scania, established in 1979. The founder and leader of the party is Carl P. Herslow.

Initially, the party sought to abolish the monopoly of the Swedish state on the radio and television market and to establish self-government for Scania. It originally advocated for full independence for Scania as a republic, but later revised this stance to support devolution within the Swedish state. From the mid-1980s, the party began to criticize Swedish immigration policy and, since the 2000s, has focused extensively on a campaign against Islam. Its support has diminished over the years, culminating in the loss of its last local seats in the 2006 Swedish general election.

parties.name: Social Democrats
parties.description:
A social democratic political party in Sweden.

Founded in 1889, the Social Democratic Party is the country's oldest and currently largest party. It has dominated the country's politics for the past century, being returned as the largest party in every election since September 1914. It led the government continuously from 1932 to 1976 and all but one term from 1982 to 2006. It is currently in opposition after the left bloc narrowly lost the 2022 election. The first female PM in Swedish history, Magdalena Andersson, is the current leader of the Social Democratic Party.

parties.name: Socialist Alternative
parties.description:
A Swedish Marxist and Trotskyist political party. The party has no party leader, but instead has a collective leadership in the Executive Committee (VU). The party is registered with the electoral authority for parliamentary elections.[3] The party is a Swedish section of the [[intISA|International Socialist Alternative]] (ISA).

The party describes itself as having been an active and sometimes leading force in various protest movements against right-wing politics during the 2000s – from the Gothenburg Action in 2001 (against the EU summit), the Alliance's changes affecting the unemployed and the sick, to the campaigns Welfare without Profit, Another Care is Possible and the Welfare Alliance against welfare gains, cuts, etc. A recurring part of the party's work is the fight against racism, but also linking this to the fight against cuts and right-wing politics, which the party believes are the breeding ground for racism. Since the 2018 election, the housing struggle has been an important part of the party's work, with active work in the campaign No to Market Rent.

parties.name: Socialist Politics
parties.relations: Ceased its activities as political party in 2019, politically merging into the [[seV|Left Party]] (V)
parties.description:
An eco-socialist association. It was previously a political party under the name Socialist Party. The organization belongs to the [[intUSFI|Fourth International]]. Socialist Politics has been registered with the electoral authority as a political party and has stood in parliamentary and municipal elections. In the fall of 2019, the Socialistiska Partiet was reorganized into the association Socialist Politics. Socialist Politics publishes a weekly magazine called Internationalen and a theoretical journal called Röda Rummet.

The [[intFI|Fourth International]] was founded in 1938 by, among others, Leon Trotsky. This is a revolutionary socialist organization, whose members want to interpret Marx primarily with the support of Lenin and Trotsky's theoretical writings and practical politics. The first Swedish section was established in 1949 when the [[seRSP|Revolutionary Socialist Party]] joined and was dissolved 3–4 years later when that party was closed down. In 1969, a Swedish section was started again, under the name Revolutionary Marxists. The organization has also been called the Revolutionary Marxist League (RMF) and the Communist Workers' League (KAF), before adopting the name Socialist Party in 1982.

In 2019, the Socialist Party was reorganized from a political party into an "eco-socialist organisation for activism and ideology production" named Socialist Politics that calls for its members to join the [[seV|Left Party]].

parties.name: SPI Welfare
parties.description:
A Swedish political party. It was founded in Malmö in 1987 and has previously primarily targeted pensioners and the disabled.

With the name change to SPI Välfärden in May 2013, the party broadened its political scope and has since then targeted all ages, under the slogan "We are all future pensioners, if we are allowed to stay alive". The development of pensions is an important element of the party's policy.

The party describes itself as "transpolitical"  and considers itself outside the right-left scale. During the 2018−2022 mandate period, the party had no mandates in either the Riksdag or any regional council, but had 3 mandates in the municipal council in Hörby municipality. The party achieved its best results in the elections of 1998, 2002 and 2006 when they had approximately 50–70 municipal mandates and 2–4 mandates in the county council in Halland.

parties.name: Sweden Democrats
parties.relations: Preceded by the [[seSveP|Sweden Party]] (SvP)
parties.description:
A nationalist and right-wing populist political party in Sweden founded in 1988. As of 2023, it is the largest member of Sweden's right-wing bloc and the second-largest party in the Riksdag. It provides confidence and supply to the right-wing ruling coalition. Within the European Union, the party is a member of the [[euECR|European Conservatives and Reformists Party]].

The party describes itself as social conservative with a nationalist foundation. The party has also been variously characterised by universities, political commentators, and international media as economic nationalist, national-conservative, anti-immigration, anti-Islam, anti-gender, Eurosceptic, and right-wing or far-right. The Sweden Democrats reject the far-right label, saying that it no longer represents its political beliefs. Among the party's founders, original leadership and early members were several people that had previously been active in white nationalist and neo-Nazi political parties and organizations. Under the leadership of Jimmie Åkesson since 2005, the SD underwent a process of reform by expelling hardline members and moderating its beliefs, building on a work that had begun during the late 1990s and early 2000s when the party began to distance itself from neo-Nazi activism and sought to position its image as a more mainstream party. Today, the SD officially rejects fascism and Nazism on their platform and since 2012 claims to have maintained a zero-tolerance policy against "extremists", "lawbreakers", and "racists". In 2025, the SD issued an official apology for its previous links to neo-Nazism during its early years.

The Sweden Democrats oppose current Swedish immigration and integration policies, instead supporting stronger restrictions on immigration and measures for immigrants to assimilate into Swedish culture. The Sweden Democrats are critical of multiculturalism and support having a common national and cultural identity, which they believe improves social cohesion. The party supports the Swedish welfare state but is against providing welfare to people who are not Swedish citizens and permanent residents of Sweden. The Sweden Democrats support a mixed market economy combining ideas from the centre-left and centre-right. The party supports same-sex marriage, civil unions for gay couples, and gender-affirming surgery but prefers that children be raised in a traditional nuclear family and argues that churches or private institutions should have the final say on performing a wedding over the state. The SD also calls for a ban on forced, polygamous or child marriages and stricter enforcement of laws against honour violence. The Sweden Democrats support keeping Sweden's nuclear power plants in order to mitigate climate change but argues that other countries should reduce their greenhouse gas emissions instead of Sweden, which the party believes is doing enough to reduce their emissions. The Sweden Democrats support generally increasing minimum sentences for crimes, as well as increasing police resources and personnel. The party also supports increasing the number of Swedish Army brigades and supports raising Sweden's defense spending.

Support for the Sweden Democrats has grown steadily since the 1990s and the party crossed the 4% threshold necessary for parliamentary representation for the first time during the 2010 Swedish general election, polling 5.7% and gaining 20 seats in the Riksdag. This increase in popularity has been compared by international media to other similar anti-immigration movements in Europe. The party received increased support in the 2018 Swedish general election, when it polled 17.5% and secured 62 seats in parliament, becoming the third largest party in Sweden. The Sweden Democrats were formerly isolated in the Riksdag until the late 2010s, with other parties maintaining a policy of refusing cooperation with them. In 2019, the leader of the [[seKD|Christian Democrats]], Ebba Busch announced that her party was ready to start negotiations with the Sweden Democrats in the Riksdag, as did [[seM|Moderate Party]] leader Ulf Kristersson. In the 2022 Swedish general election, the party ran as part of a broad right-wing alliance with those two parties and the [[seL|Liberals]], and came second overall with 20.5% of the vote. Following the election and the Tidö Agreement, it was negotiated that SD agreed to support a Moderate Party-led government together with the Christian Democrats and the Liberals. It is the first time that SD holds direct influence over the government.

parties.name: Sweden Party
parties.relations:
Merger of the [[seBSS|Bevara Sverige Svenskt]] (BSS) and the Stockholm branch of [[seFsP|Progress Party]];

Succeeded by the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] (SD)
parties.description:
A far-right political party in Sweden. It was founded in late 1986 through the merger of [[seBSS|Bevara Sverige Svenskt]] and the Stockholm branch of the [[seFsP|Progress Party]]. The leader of the party was Stefan Herrmann, formerly the leader of the Progress Party.

In October 1987, Herrmann was expelled from the party. His group reconstituted the Progress Party. The remainder of the party would regroup as the Sweden Democrats in 1988.

The Sweden Party was formed in 1986 after a meeting in Stockholm. Its founders included Stefan Hermann, Leif Zeilon and Sven Davidson who were active in the Bevara Sverige Svenskt organization. The party never officially ran for election and during the 1988 Swedish general election advocated boycotting the main parties, stating "DO NOT VOTE for the traitors in the 1988 election" and used symbols associated with white power movements. The party was formally dissolved in 1988, with some of its members playing a role in the founding of the [[seSD|Sweden Democrats]] which emerged as a successor.
parties.ideology: In its policies, the Sweden Party was critical of immigration into Sweden and argued that a market economy was superior to a planned economy, but also advocated for certain protectionist measures such as limiting the power of foreign companies in Sweden and breaking up what it called the "power of big finance." Swedish historian Heléne Lööw has argued that the Sweden Party did not hold a coherent ideology and was internally polarized between two groups; those sympathetic to national socialist and neo-Nazi ideas and a more conventional right-wing populist and national conservative faction.

parties.name: Swedish Social Democratic Left Party
parties.relations:
Split from the [[seV|Swedish Social Democratic Left Party]] (SSV);

Merged into the [[seSAP|Swedish Social Democratic Workers' Party]] (SAP)
parties.description:
A short-lived political party, formed on 25 March 1921 as a breakaway from the original [[seV|Swedish Social Democratic Left Party]], formed in 1917. When the original SSV accepted the "21 Theses" of the [[seComintern|Third International]] (Comintern) and changed its name to the Swedish Communist Party (SKP), non-revolutionary elements were excluded. These, approximately 6,000 people, regrouped in the new SSV. The leader of the new party was Ivar Vennerström.

Västerbottens Folkblad was one of the party's newspapers. The party's members of parliament belonged to the social democratic left group.

Vennerström's SSV participated in the 1921 Second Chamber election (received 3.2%) and the 1922 municipal election (1.8%).

In international affairs, the SSV joined the work of the Vienna International. After many parties within the Vienna International in other countries in Europe merged with those in the Second International, an opinion arose in the autumn of 1922 that this should also happen in Sweden. The SSV and the [[seSAP|Social Democratic Workers' Party]] (SAP) met for discussions about this in November 1922, and the merger itself took place in the first half of 1923.

parties.relations:
Split from the [[seSNSP|Swedish National Socialist Party]] (SNSP);

Succeeded by the [[seNRP|Nordic Realm Party]] (NRP)
parties.description:
A Swedish political party that initially espoused Nazism before adopting a more indigenous form of fascism. The party was generally among the public called Lindholmarna (lit. 'the Lindholm-ers', after their leader Sven Olov Lindholm).

The party was revealed after WWII to have had well-organized plans, containing death lists of local Jews to be rounded up and deported and also plans for the construction of two Swedish concentration camps, in case of a Nazi German invasion of Sweden. Lindholm himself had planned to take the role as a "Swedish Quisling" if such an invasion had happened.

The Swedish king Gustav V had friendly ties to the SSS/NSAP during the war.

The party was revealed after WWII to have had well-organized plans, containing death lists of local Jews to be rounded up and deported and also plans for the construction of two Swedish concentration camps, in case of a Nazi German invasion of Sweden. Lindholm himself had planned to take the role as a "Swedish Quisling" if such an invasion had happened.

The Swedish king Gustav V had friendly ties to the SSS/NSAP during the war.

parties.name: Swedish Socialist Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seV|Communist Party of Sweden]] (SKP)
parties.description:
A political party in Sweden active from 1929 to 1948. Led by Karl Kilbom and Nils Flyg, the party was founded in 1929 as a splinter group of the [[seV|Communist Party of Sweden]]. Until 1934, the splinter group used the same name as the old party, the Communist Party of Sweden (Swedish: Sveriges kommunistiska parti), so in order to keep the two factions apart, this faction was generally known as Kilbommare ("Kilbomiars") while those who stayed in the old party were known as Sillénare ("Sillénians", after their leader Hugo Sillén).

In the split, the entire communist parliamentary group, the party's official newspaper, Folkets Dagblad Politiken, and most of the more militant members joined the Kilbom-Flyg faction.

The Kilbom-led SKP held its congress prior to the Sillén-led party. At the congress there was a debate regarding the character of the party, whether to continue the system of party cells (the structure of the pre-split SKP) or whether to become a more open mass party. In the end the statutes adopted by the congress differed little from those of the pre-split SKP. Party cells remained the basic organization of the party, and in places where no cell existed a party member would be organized in the arbetarkommun directly. However the criteria for membership were relaxed, the sole remaining criterion was activism in the base level organization.

In 1930, Flyg, as an MP, put forward a motion on separation of church and state. The motion was voted down in the Lower House.

The Kilbom party merged in 1934 with a break-away group of the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]] based in Gothenburg, led by Albin Ström. At the time of the merger, the party changed its name to the Socialist Party (Socialistiska partiet). The transformation into SP also marked a break with the previous line of the party towards the [[intComintern|Comintern]] and the Soviet Union. Initially the party had tried to persuade the Comintern to be allowed to return to the International. Gradually, however the party became more and more antagonistic toward the Comintern and the Soviet Union.

The party gradually disintegrated, and many of the most prominent leaders such as Kilbom, left the party in 1937. During World War II, their staunch anti-Soviet line led the party to actually embrace some pro-German views (partially since the huge financial problems of the party led it to seek financial aid from Germany). As a result of this, in 1940, a group of members that included Albin Ström and Evald Höglund broke away and formed the [[seVSP|Left Socialist Party]]. In the elections the same year, the party lost its parliamentary representation.

When Flyg died in 1943, he was succeeded as party leader by Agaton Blom. During the final years of the war, the party continued to lose members and support, and changed its name to the Swedish Socialist Party (Svenska socialistiska partiet), which was outspokenly supportive of Nazi ideology. The Swedish Socialist Party participated in the 1944 election and received 5,279 votes or 2 per thousand; they probably never reached a thousand members. The party was disbanded in 1948.

The local units of the party were known as "Socialist Labour Communes" (Socialistiska Arbetarkommuner).

In terms of international contacts, the party was initially associated with the [[intICO|International Communist Opposition]] and later with the [[intIRMC|International Revolutionary Marxist Centre]] (also known as the "London Bureau").

The youth league of the party was called the Socialist Youth League (Socialistiska ungdomsförbundet), affiliated to the International Bureau of Revolutionary Youth Organizations.

parties.name: The New Party
parties.description:
A political party founded by Ian Wachtmeister in the spring of 1998 and which ran in the 1998 parliamentary election.

The party program had many similarities to [[seNyD|New Democracy]], such as tax cuts, privatizations, restrictive immigration policies, and conservative family policies. After the election, where (d) received barely half a percent of the vote (25,276 votes), the party was dissolved, but the party name was still registered for the 2006 election. One of the party's slogans was "Both seals and people need nuclear power".

Ian Wachtmeister blamed the party's poor election results on the media's silence.

The new party's logo was a fusion of a d and a proboscis-a. Because of this, a conflict arose between The New Party and the Swedish Data Protection Authority, which had a similar logo.

The new party released the campaign song "Say yes to the future", which was played at various town hall meetings during the 1998 election campaign. The song was written by Ian Wachtmeister himself but never became as popular as New Democracy's party song "Häng Med-Häng Med", which was written by Paul Paljett before the 1991 election.

parties.name: United Right Party
parties.relations: Merged into [[seFKNP|First Chamber National Party]]
parties.description: A political party in the first chamber of the Swedish Riksdag during the period 1888–1911. The party had a unifying message of tariff friendliness, and because it united a large majority of the members of the first chamber, it was also called the Protectionist Majority Party, the Great Party or just the First Chamber's Majority Party. In 1910 the party changed its name to the United Right Party, and in 1912 it became part of the [[seFKNP|First Chamber's National Party]], which in turn became part of the [[seM|Right Party]] in 1935.
parties.ideology:
After a meeting on January 15, 1910, party chairman Ernst Trygger summarized the party's tasks:
"Our party wants to characterize itself as a modern right, with an open eye for the needs of the times, unafraid to take up the knife to cut away what is rotten in society, but with reverent tenderness preserving the priceless values ​​that we possess in our homeland, our spiritual and our material culture."

parties.name: United Socialists
parties.relations: Merged into the [[seAL|Workers' List]] (AL)
parties.description:
A local political party registered for election to the municipal council in Gällivare municipality. It started as a collaboration between the [[seKFML|Solidarity Party]], the [[seSF|Socialist League]] and the [[seMAF|Malmfälten Workers' Association]] (MAF). The Solidarity Party left the collaboration after the 1988 elections. The party was represented in the Gällivare municipal council during the 1988/1991 term.

On 9 December 1989, a founding meeting was held to become a nationwide party. The party then consisted of three groups: the International Group, the MAF and the Marxist-Leninist League. In early 1990, the United Socialists decided to dissolve in order to join the [[seAL|Workers' List]].

parties.name: Unity
parties.description: A small political party in Sweden. The party was founded on 6 April 1990 on the initiative of Ulf Wåhlström. It started with some influences from New Age and spirituality, but is nowadays a political party mostly focused on the environment, an unconditional income floor with a basic income and alternative medicine. The party has taken part in every national election in Sweden since 1991, mostly with limited success. The 2014 general election was the party's best result so far, with 0.1% of the total votes. In the 2018 Swedish general election, the party received 0.06% of the total votes.

parties.name: Unity Party
parties.relations: Split from the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]].
parties.description:
Jamal El-Haj has been a member of the Riksdag for the [[seSAP|Social Democratic Party]] since 2018, being re-elected in 2022. In the spring of 2023, El-Haj caused a controversy when, despite his party's advice, he participated in a Palestine conference with links to the [[psHamas|Hamas]] movement.

On 7 February 2024, a leaked document revealed El-Haj's attempt to use his position in the Riksdag to influence the Swedish Migration Agency regarding the asylum application of a controversial conservative Muslim Egyptian imam. Furthermore, it was revealed that he had asked the agency to conceal his attempts to influence the decision. Following widespread public outcry, on 9 February 2024, the Social Democratic Party declared a loss of confidence in El-Haj and demanded his resignation from Riksdag. El-Haj left the party but retained his seat as an independent.

In early 2024, El-Haj rejected an attempt to recruit him from the [[seNyP|Nuance Party]].

In July 2025, it was reported that El-Haj had gathered associations and imams in support of the Unity Party, which had already submitted an application to the Election Authority in mid-June. One of the meetings Jamal El-Haj held was with the Iraq Turkmen Peace Association in Malmö. The party was co-founded by Ana Sarmiento Sánchez, a doctor who describes herself as "dissatisfied with the current party politics." It was reported that about 100 people from different cultural and religious backgrounds participated in the creation of the party.

On 30 August 2025, the Swedish Arabic-language newspaper Alkompis reported that Jamal El-Haj publicly announced the launch of his Unity Party in Malmö at a meeting attended by approximately 80 people. Earlier, on 12 August 2025, the Election Authority registered notice of participation of the Unity Party in the 2026 Swedish general election, the 2029 European Parliament election, as well as 2026 regional and local elections. The party published its 17-point program on Instagram and announced its participation in the 2026 elections.

On 18 February 2026, El-Haj announced on his Facebook page that the Unity Party would not participate in the 2026 elections at any level. He stated that in recent months, many party members had been "exposed to repeated attacks and questioning that have damaged both us and the democratic conversation." According to El-Haj, he will remain in Riksdag until the end of his term in September, and that the Unity Party will aim for the next EU and 2030 general elections.
parties.ideology:
According to the party program, it has four core values: international solidarity, humanism, economic equality and climate responsibility. The Unity Party describes itself as pro-immigration, stating that "Sweden needs more immigration - not less." The party also highlights one of its goals as combating the hatred directed against Muslims, "a situation that is often overlooked." According to the party's co-founder and vice president, Ana Sarmiento Sánchez, the party's core values are human rights, equality and social justice, sustainable development and environmental responsibility, international solidarity and global cooperation, democracy and openness, economic justice and equality.

Sánchez stated that the Unity Party stands as a counterpoint to the right-wing wave in Sweden, as in the rest of the Western world.
