parties.name: Workers' List
parties.relations: Merger of the [[seFS|United Socialists]], [[seSF|Socialist League]], and splinter groups from [[seSAP|Social Democrats]] and [[seKFML|Communist Party of Sweden]].
parties.description:
A Swedish political party, registered for elections with the electoral authority until 2006.

The decision to found the Workers' List party was taken on 21 January 1990 at a meeting in Uppsala by around 20 union activists who had been involved in the Dala Appeal in the previous years. Among these was Åke Wiklund, who had been chairman of the workshop club within the Metall union at Saab-Scania in Falun and in 1985 was one of the founders of the Dala Appeal. At the meeting, a temporary board was appointed for the first congress. The constituent congress was held at Vasa Gymnasium in Stockholm on 19 May 1990. The party had a very loose composition, and recruited its members from various organizations within the labor movement. The intention was to form a party for dissatisfied social democratic voters. Many of the party's most leading figures came from the Maoist party [[seKFML|SKP]], including Lars Aronsson, Kjell Eriksson and Jörgen Larsson, or from the Trotskyist organization [[seSF|Socialist League]] and [[seFS|United Socialists]], but the majority of its members came from the [[seSAP|Social Democrats]].

However, the party split before the 1991 election, and ultimately the remnants of the party received only 0.07 percent of the vote in the parliamentary election that year. Some who had been members of the party later formed the [[seFDEM|Popular Democrats]]. Even Åke Wiklund, who was elected party chairman in 1991 distanced himself from the Workers' List in 1993. He believed that the party was aimed at social democrats and was being taken over by the "the crazy lefists". The Workers' List did, however, receive some local representation; in both Ragunda Municipality and Timrå Municipality, the party received 1 seat on the municipal council in the 1991 elections, and in Vimmerby Municipality, the Workers' List received 1 seat on the municipal council in the three following elections in 1994, 1998 and 2002.

The party received 102 votes in the 1998 parliamentary election and 12 votes in the 2002 parliamentary election. The party also ran in the 1995 European Parliament election. The party did not run in the 2006 parliamentary election. The party name was deregistered in 2006.

parties.literalName: Movement of the Reformists of Tajikistan
parties.description:
A Tajik opposition political movement, the creation of which was announced in August 2025. According to the official statement of its founders, the movement advocates for political reform, democratization of public administration, protection of civil liberties, and opposition to authoritarianism in Tajikistan.

The movement's creation was announced on 6 August 2025, in an official statement by its founders and organizing committee. The document noted that a significant portion of the movement's members reside outside Tajikistan as political refugees. At a joint meeting of the founders, the organizing committee, and foreign representative offices, Muhammadikboli Sadriddin was elected as the leader of the movement.

According to the statement, the decision to establish the movement was made after the formation of the organizing committee and a network of representative offices abroad.

According to the founders' official statement, the movement declares the following goals: carrying out political reforms; ensuring free and competitive elections; holding government bodies accountable; protecting civil liberties; fighting corruption; ensuring citizens' equality before the law.
The movement also declared its readiness to cooperate with other opposition forces in Tajikistan.

According to the statement, the decision to establish the movement was made after the formation of the organizing committee and a network of representative offices abroad.

According to the founders' official statement, the movement declares the following goals: carrying out political reforms; ensuring free and competitive elections; holding government bodies accountable; protecting civil liberties; fighting corruption; ensuring citizens' equality before the law.
The movement also declared its readiness to cooperate with other opposition forces in Tajikistan.

parties.relations: Two-month cancelled merger of the [[trSCP|Socialist Republican Party]] (SCP) and the [[tr1920TKP|Socialist Liberation Party]] (1920 TKP).
parties.description:
On 14 August 2023, it was announced that two Turkish left-wing parties, the [[trSCP|Socialist Republican Party]] (SCP) and the [[tr1920TKP|Socialist Liberation Party]] (1920 TKP), had decided to merge to form the Socialist Party of Turkey (TSP) on 9 September 2023. The press called the merger of the two parties "unexpected."

On 9 September 2023, a unification congress of the party was held in Ankara. Yılmaz Ersezer from the [[trSCP|SCP]] became the party's chairman, and İsmail Kaplan from the [[tr1920TKP|1290 TKP]] became the secretary general.

Two months later, on 9 November 2023, the [[tr1920TKP|Socialist Liberation Party]] announced in X: "Unfortunately, we were unable to complete our unity in the areas of organizational principles and party work among the masses." Both parties announced an "amicable separation" and that they would again operate independenrly.
parties.ideology:
On 9 September 2023, at a congress in Ankara, TSP Chairman Yılmaz Ersezer stated: "The SCP and the 1920 TKP have united, taking into account the grave conditions in Turkey and the world and heeding the call of our people 'not to divide, but to unite.' We will withdraw from NATO, we will seize American bases. We will establish a completely independent Turkey. We will put an end to sectarianism by applying the laws of the Republic. We will close the doors of the Middle Ages, never to be reopened. We will eradicate hostility towards women and children. We will transition to a planned economy for national development. We will eliminate unemployment, high prices, and poverty. We will end the tyranny of one man. We will establish the sovereignty of the people against the imperialist and capitalist tyranny, which is the basis of the tyranny of one man. We want a revolution in Turkey, a revolution in the region, a revolution in the entire world."

The TSP advocates withdrawal from NATO and the seizure of American bases. The TSP also seeks to end the existence of religious sects and eradicate hatred against women and children. The TSP advocates the unification of socialist and Kemalist ideas, expressed in the ideology of a "national democratic revolution."
